messages:
carmen: Quick flag — onboarding run for llama3p (fp16 -> nf4) shows a weird regression on our long-context chat eval (drop in coherence after ~6k tokens). filing notes here so we don't lose it.

jess: ugh. is that the same pattern as the earlier kv-wrap bug? or a tokenizer shift?

carmen: looks different. tokens line up but responses start repeating older context. kv cache seems to re-use keys for new positions? logs attached below.

kyle: can you paste the smallest repro? i can run a bisect on the runtime change that landed last week.

maria: quick data: nf4 quant on cpu/gpu both. baseline fp16 vs nf4 perplexity delta small on short contexts, but long-context rouge and prompt-follow score tank. here's snippet from eval harness: 

```
# run: eval_longcontext --model=llama3p-nf4 --ctx=8192 --promptset=chat-e2e
INFO: seq_at_6144: loss=3.2, repeat_rate=0.12
INFO: seq_at_6650: loss=4.8, repeat_rate=0.47  <-- sharp jump
KV_CACHE: observed duplicate key ids at positions 6650..6672
```

jess: duplicate key ids — that smells like a token-id -> kv-index aliasing or a head-dim offset issue when computing rope. did we change per-head split mapping in the conversion?

carmen: conversion script for the new checkpoint did have a nonstandard head-split option (headwise_phase_split=True) to match original ckpt layout. i ran a quick token map diff and saw head offsets differ by +128 for some heads.

kyle: ok that matches a theory: if rotary (or rope) application uses a per-head offset that doesn't match kv cache packing order, the same cache index could be overwritten for a different token position. gives duplicate key ids.

maria: also noticed tokenizer normalization difference between the upstream repo and our conversion — upstream does NFKC normalization, our saved tokenizer had do_normalize=false. could cause token id shifts for some combined chars in long-form text and change the stream boundaries.

carmen: reproducer that showed both effects: run with our tokenizer + head-split mapping -> fails; enforce do_normalize=true on tokenizer then rerun -> still fails but duplicate key ids pattern changes. so two orthogonal issues.

```
# quick diff we saw in tokenizer.json
- "do_normalize": false
+ "do_normalize": true
  "normalization_form": "NFKC"
```

jess: good find. action items: (1) lock tokenizer normalization to NFKC during conversion, (2) audit head packing order in conversion mapping, (3) add regression test in long-context harness that checks for duplicate KV ids. i can take (3).

kyle: i'll bisect the conversion scripts vs latest runtime change. initial hunch is conversion introduced headwise split with inconsistent packing. will try reverting head-split option and re-export.

maria: i ran a quick quant check: nf4 vs int8 on 8k context — nf4 had slightly better token-likelihood but worse repeat_rate when the kv collisions happen. so quant interacts with the failure mode (maybe numerical noise hides it sometimes). logs: 

```
Model    | avg_loss_4k | avg_loss_8k | repeat_rate_8k
fp16     | 2.9         | 3.0         | 0.08
nf4      | 3.0         | 4.6         | 0.45
int8     | 3.2         | 3.3         | 0.10
```

carmen: thanks. i've created a minimal gist with the converter flags and a small repro prompt. linking here: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-llama3p-kv-collision 

ci-bot: CI run queued: https://ci.redwood.ai/12345 (includes conversion smoke and long-context test).

jess: if kyle can confirm conversion mapping, we can hotfix and re-run quant sweep. for now, pls avoid promoting the nf4 build to the dedicated pool. :warning:

kyle: started local export revert, will ping when i have a candidate artifact.

maria: i'll add a check in the eval harness to assert no duplicate key ids and fail the job, plus a tokenizer normalization test.

carmen: plan: kyle fixes mapping -> maria/jen run quant + longcontext suite -> jess adds guard -> re-promote. filing GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/789 (summary + repro).

jess: nice. also add a short blurb to onboarding checklist: "verify tokenizer normalization matches upstream and verify head packing order mapping". saves future churn. :+1:

carmen: thanks team. keeping thread for updates.
